texts: Beneath the silent stars a hand reached down unasked, and lifted me from where my own strength had failed.
Write a doha about a man lost in the dark who had done everything he could, and then, under the stars, felt an unseen mercy lift him up without his asking, to a place his effort never could.
stars doha about being rescued by God's mercy when you didn't deserve it
stars, unasked mercy
I failed every attempt to climb out of debt by my own hard work, and then, one night under the stars, an old friend I hadn't spoken to in years called and cleared the entire amount.
forest doha about the Lord's mercy finding you when you were lost
Compose a doha about a traveller lost deep in a forest who had no map and no strength, and who was suddenly guided out by a mercy he never asked for and could never have earned.
forest, grace found me
Lost in the forest of my own making, I was found by a mercy that came to me before I ever called.
I was lost on a hill trek in a dense forest with a dead phone and no energy left, when a shepherd I had never met appeared and walked me out without a word.
After years of trying to cure my son's illness with every remedy, a doctor we had never heard of appeared at our gate, treated him free, and he got better; we still cannot explain it.
unearned mercy, lifted up
doha on how effort wasn't enough but the Lord's kindness lifted me anyway
My hands had failed to lift me; then the Lord's own hand came down, unasked, and raised me.
Please write a doha about the Lord's mercy that lifts a person up without being asked, doing what no amount of effort, skill or merit could do, so that the one lifted can only bow in wonder.
doha on grace - how God lifts you without you asking
I want a doha about the grace of the Lord that comes unasked, picking up the fallen and the undeserving, and doing for them what a lifetime of striving and cleverness could never accomplish.
grace, unasked, undeserved
I never prayed much, never earned anything, and yet when my life seemed ruined, an unexpected chain of kindness from strangers set me back on my feet.
Not by my merit but by Your mercy, Lord, the fallen one stands and the lost one is found.
thread doha about God's mercy pulling you through when your effort fell short
Write a doha about a thin thread that held a falling man, which he had never made and could not have trusted, and let it say that this is how the Lord's mercy catches the fallen without being asked.
My thin thread of savings could not have covered my mother's operation, yet the hospital waived everything, and the surgeon said he felt he should, without any reason.
A single thread of mercy held me when every cord of effort snapped beneath my weight.
thread, mercy, lifted
leaf doha about being carried by God's grace like a leaf on the wind
leaf, carried by grace
I applied to forty places and got no reply, then one morning a leaf-green envelope arrived from a company I never applied to, offering me exactly the job I needed.
Compose a doha about a leaf that falls on the wind and is carried safely across the water by an unseen hand, as the Lord's grace carries the soul where its own effort could never reach.
A leaf with no oar, no wings, no plan, carried across by the Lord's own breath.
I trained for a decade and failed the test of a touchstone-level exam each time, and then they changed the rules that year and I passed without trying, and I feel it was simply given.
touchstone, grace of the Lord
The touchstone tests the worth of my deeds and finds them wanting, yet Your mercy lifts me beyond my worth.
Please write a doha about a touchstone that finds a man's merit lacking, and the Lord's unasked mercy that raises him anyway, so that what effort could never earn comes freely as a gift.
touchstone doha about mercy lifting you even though you don't deserve it
oil press, mercy lifted me
Write a doha about a soul crushed like grain in an oil press, with no strength of its own left, who is suddenly lifted out by the Lord's mercy without ever asking for it.
doha with an oil press about God rescuing you when life was crushing you
The oil press that employed my father closed down, and just as we were about to lose everything, a stranger offered him a job that paid twice as much.
Pressed and pressed by the oil press of the world, I was lifted by a mercy I did not ask for.
doha about how God's grace comes without being asked
Before the plea rose in my throat, Your mercy was already on its way, Beloved.
Before I could even decide how to ask for help, my sister showed up with exactly what I needed and said she just had a feeling.
unasked mercy, divine grace
I would like a doha about the Lord's mercy that reaches a person before he even asks, like a mother who knows her child's need, doing what no striving of the child could do.
I did everything right for years, and nothing worked, but then one unexpected conversation changed my whole path, and I can only describe it as being picked up by a hand I could not see.
lifted by mercy, undeserved
Compose a doha about a person who strove and failed for years, then found himself lifted up in a single moment by a mercy he had neither earned nor requested, and can only bow in gratitude.
doha on being lifted by God's kindness after all my own efforts failed
Years of my labour could not shift the boulder; one moment of Your mercy lifted it away.
When my father lost his business, a rival we had always feared quietly paid his debts and never asked for a word of thanks, and my father said it felt like the hand of God.
The fallen did not call, the Lord did not wait; the mercy came unbidden, and the dust became a throne.
Please write a doha about the Lord's mercy that lifts a fallen man up from the dust without being asked, and about how the man can claim no credit, since his own effort had failed.
divine mercy, unasked help
doha on how God's mercy lifts us up without asking for anything
moneylender, mercy, lifted
The moneylender hounds the debtor, but the Lord's mercy forgives what no payment ever could.
Write a doha about a poor man in the grip of a moneylender with no way to pay, until a mercy he never asked for cancels everything and sets him free, as the Lord's grace frees the soul.
A moneylender had seized our family's land, and the day before the deadline, a mysterious donor repaid every rupee; to this day no one knows who it was.
moneylender doha about God clearing a debt you could never pay
After a lifetime chasing the wide ocean and the lotus of calm in meditation, I felt a stillness arrive one evening on its own, unearned, as if lowered into my hands.
ocean, lotus, divine grace
doha with ocean and lotus about grace giving what effort can't
The ocean opened and the lotus bloomed, not by my pulling, but by the Lord's gentle hand.
Please write a doha about the lotus that blooms on the ocean of the world, not through its own effort but through the grace of the morning light, as the Lord's mercy lifts the soul to bloom.
peacock, leaf, grace
Compose a doha about a peacock whose feathers shine not by its own effort, and a leaf which falls where it is carried, both showing how the Lord's grace gives beauty and shelter freely.
peacock and leaf doha about God's grace raising you up
The peacock did not paint its feathers, the leaf did not choose its landing; all is gift of Your grace.
The peacock in our garden hatched in the leaf-litter though everyone said the eggs were dead, and I took it as a sign that grace works where effort has given up.
Write a doha about an iron bar hammered in the furnace which cannot make itself precious, and about the Lord's grace that transforms the soul without its own effort.
My craft shop's furnace broke down just before the biggest order of my life, and a neighbour I barely knew lent his own for free, saving the whole business.
The furnace heats and the hammer falls, but only the Lord's grace turns the iron into something holy.
furnace, divine grace
doha with a furnace about grace doing what effort can't
leaf, grace, lifted
A fallen leaf lifted by the breeze, a fallen soul lifted by grace: neither asked, both were raised.
Please write a doha about a dry leaf lifted by the wind high above where it fell, and how the Lord's mercy raises the fallen soul in the same way, without being asked or earned.
leaf doha about God lifting you up for no reason
I felt like a dry leaf blown about after my divorce, and then a series of quiet strokes of luck lifted me up, one after another, without my doing anything.
Write a doha about a man who weighs his good deeds on scales and finds them light, and about his shadow growing long, until the Lord's mercy lifts him to where no weight of merit could carry him.
scales and shadow doha - God's grace goes beyond what we deserve
The scales say I am light, the shadow says I am small, and still the Lord's mercy lifts me.
When I weighed my good deeds against my mistakes the scales tipped badly, and my shadow looked longer than ever that evening, but my friend forgave everything and welcomed me back.
scales, shadow, grace
After a lifetime of failures on my own, the thing that finally saved me was a kindness from a stranger that I did nothing to deserve.
grace beyond effort
I want a doha that says that the highest things, peace, freedom and the sight of the divine, cannot be earned by effort alone, but come as gifts of the Lord's mercy to those who simply remain open.
What the labouring hand cannot reach, the Lord's mercy places gently in the open palm.
doha about things that effort alone can't achieve but God's mercy gives
I tried to stop drinking for fifteen years through willpower, rehab and promises, and then one morning I woke up and the craving was simply gone, which I can only call being let off.
Please write a doha about a man who fought his weakness for years by his own will and failed, then was freed in a moment by a mercy he did not seek, as if the Lord had lifted a weight.
The chain I could not break fell off one morning, unasked, by the quiet kindness of the Lord.
freed by mercy
doha about the Lord freeing you from something you couldn't beat yourself
The pot of water that I could not fill was filled by the Lord's rain, unasked.
The pot of water in our village had been empty for three summers, and then rain came on its own the night we gave up hoping, and the tank brimmed over.
pot of water, grace
Compose a doha about a pot of water that no human effort could fill, and the Lord's mercy that fills it overnight without being asked, as it fills the empty soul with what effort never could.
pot of water doha about God's mercy filling what I couldn't
The prayer beads my grandmother left me are worn smooth, but she said she never earned anything with them, and the palace-sized joys of her life simply came as a gift.
doha with prayer beads and a palace about God's grace over my own efforts
prayer beads, palace, mercy
In the palace of merit, count the prayer beads as you will; the Lord's mercy needs no counting.
Write a doha about a man who counts his prayer beads and builds himself a palace of merit, and about the Lord's mercy that lifts the poorest soul beyond all counting, without being earned.

I would like a doha for someone who believes he earned everything by hard work, reminding him that every breath, every meeting and every blessing is a gift of the Lord's mercy, unasked and undeserved.
doha on how everything good that came to me was a gift, not earned
Not one good thing in my life was earned; each was a petal dropped by the Lord's passing mercy.
Looking back at my career, I see that every big break came from a stranger's unexpected kindness and not from my planning, and it humbles me.
everything is a gift
My father's cancer went into remission after the doctors had given up hope, and the oncologist simply shrugged and said it was beyond medicine.
doha about God's mercy doing the impossible when doctors gave up
Please write a doha about an illness that all human skill had given up on, which was lifted by the Lord's mercy without any asking, to show that grace does what no skill or striving can.
beyond medicine, divine grace
When the healer's hands had fallen still, a greater Hand moved, and the sick one rose.
philosopher's stone and tortoise doha - God's grace transforms what effort can't
My slow little tortoise somehow survived a harsh winter outdoors, and my grandfather, who hunted for a philosopher's stone in his youth, said true transformation is always a gift.
philosopher's stone, tortoise, grace

Write a doha about a slow tortoise that could never run to the goal, and a philosopher's stone that transforms without being sought, showing that the Lord's grace brings what pace and striving never can.
The tortoise could never run, but grace carried it; the philosopher's stone cannot be found, but grace gives it.
The church bell at the harbour rang just as the ocean calmed, after a night when our fishing family had given up hope, and my mother wept saying she had not even prayed.
bell and ocean doha about God's mercy saving you unasked
Compose a doha about a sailor on a stormy ocean who has given up hope and prayer, and then hears a bell calling through the dark and is saved by a mercy that came unasked.
bell, ocean, unasked mercy
The ocean raged, the bell tolled, and the Lord's mercy found us before we thought to call.
diamond, beggar, grace
diamond and beggar doha about God's mercy lifting the poor man up
Write a doha about a beggar who finds a diamond at his feet that he never searched for, and let it say that this is how the Lord's grace comes, unasked, to the humblest soul.
A beggar outside our colony found a diamond ring in the dust one morning, returned it, and was rewarded with a room and a job; he called it God's doing, not his.
The beggar asked for bread, and Your mercy handed him a diamond; so lavish is Your grace.
The stars did not strive to shine, the diamond did not strive to glitter; so the Lord gives beauty by grace alone.
diamond, stars, grace
I gazed at a diamond ring in a shop window under a sky full of stars and thought how none of my efforts had earned me the love I now have, which just arrived.

Please write a doha about a diamond that glitters without trying and stars that shine without striving, showing that the Lord's grace gives its gifts freely, and that no effort of ours could earn them.
diamond and stars doha about grace, you can't earn it
diamond, grace
The diamond came from darkness and pressure, not from its own will; so grace comes from the Lord's will alone.
I found out last week that my mother had sold her only diamond to cover my school fees without telling me, a mercy I will never be able to repay.
Compose a doha about a diamond formed in darkness by forces it never chose, and how the Lord's mercy shapes the soul in the same way, with no effort or merit of its own.
diamond doha about God's grace being a gift you can't earn
My neighbour never goes to any gathering or reads any scripture, yet his life has been quietly rescued time and again, and he credits only kindness from above.
Neither penance nor purse could buy it; the Lord gave His mercy because that is His nature.
doha on how God's mercy can't be bought or earned by penance
I want a doha that says no penance, no rituals, no gifts or cleverness can purchase the Lord's mercy, which is given freely by Him alone to whomever He chooses, unasked and without price.
mercy, unearned, unbought
shadow and blind man doha - God's mercy shows the way
My blind uncle, who has lived in shadow all his life, was led across a flooded street by a child he did not know, and he said that was God's hand.
Write a doha about a blind man in deep shadow who is led safely by an unseen hand he never requested, as the Lord's mercy leads the soul where its own effort would have failed.
shadow, blind man, grace
The blind man walks in shadow, yet a Hand he never saw leads him, unasked, to the light.
Compose a doha about a blind man who plants a seed and cannot see it grow, yet the Lord's mercy makes it blossom, showing how grace completes what effort began and could not finish.
My blind friend planted a seed in a pot as a hobby and forgot it for months; one morning it had grown into a full plant, and he said it was a gift he did not deserve.
seed, blind man, grace
The blind man sowed, the seed grew unseen, and Your mercy, Lord, did the rest.
doha with a seed and a blind man about God's grace growing things we can't
After I lost my savings, my ex-boss, a man I once quarrelled with, called out of the blue and offered me a position with no interview, and I still cannot account for it.
Please write a doha about the Lord's mercy that finds a person after he has given up on himself and everyone else, lifting him up unasked, and doing what no effort of his could ever do.
doha on mercy arriving after you've given up
When I had stopped asking, the answer came; such is the unbidden mercy of the Lord.
mercy after giving up
bridge, divine mercy
I stood at the broken bridge with empty hands, and the Lord's mercy laid a plank across the gulf.
The bridge to our village was washed away and I had no way to reach my sick mother, until a farmer I had never met rowed me across without being asked.
bridge doha about God's grace carrying you across when you couldn't cross yourself
Write a doha about a bridge that collapses beneath a wayfarer who has no means to cross, and the Lord's mercy that lifts him over to the far side, doing what no effort of his could do.
Not for my prayers, not for my penance, but for His own sweet nature the Lord lifts the lowly.
I would like a doha about how the Lord lifts up even the lowly and the unworthy out of pure kindness, and that no one can claim the gift as wages for his effort, however hard he has worked.
mercy for the unworthy
doha: God lifts people up out of pure kindness, not because they earned it
When I was at my worst, behaving terribly to everyone, my sister still stood by me and nursed me back, and I realised that is the closest thing to divine mercy I have seen.
In the noisy market of deeds, the thorn of failure pricks us all; yet the Lord's mercy heals what no bargain could.
Compose a doha about a market where everything is bought and sold by merit, and a thorn of failure in the foot of a man who cannot pay, whom the Lord's mercy heals freely without a price.
market and thorn doha - grace is free, you can't buy it
I wandered through the market with a thorn in my foot and not a coin in my pocket, until a shopkeeper bandaged me, fed me and refused any payment.
market, thorn, free mercy
The traveler has no strength to walk to the sandalwood grove, yet its fragrance comes to meet him; so does the Lord's grace.
sandalwood, traveler, grace
sandalwood and traveler doha - grace finds you without being sought
Write a doha about a tired traveler who cannot reach a distant sandalwood grove, but whom the fragrance of grace reaches on the wind, lifting his spirit without any effort of his own.
On a long walk, a traveler worn out and ready to quit, I caught the smell of sandalwood incense from a stranger's courtyard, and an unexplained surge of hope carried me onward.
fire doha about God's mercy saving someone from burning
Please write a doha about a man trapped in the fire of his own mistakes, who cannot put it out by effort, and who is suddenly drawn out by a mercy he never requested, and can only weep in thanks.
When fire broke out in our building at night, a neighbour I barely knew carried my mother down the stairs and disappeared before I could thank him.
The fire of my deeds was burning high, but Your mercy, unasked, drew me out through the smoke.
fire, mercy, unasked
At the crossroads, lost and weary, I found no sign but a gentle Hand turning me toward the way.
crossroads, grace guides
I stood at a crossroads in my life with no idea which way to go, and then a chance meeting at a bus stop pointed me right to the answer.
crossroads doha about God's grace guiding you unasked
Compose a doha about a lost man at a crossroads, with no signs and no strength to choose, who is gently turned the right way by the Lord's mercy, without his asking or knowing.
leaf and one-string lute doha - grace carries you
Write a doha about a falling leaf and a wandering singer with a one-string lute who owns nothing, both carried through life by the Lord's mercy, which gives them all they need without being asked.
leaf, one-string lute, grace
The street singer with a one-string lute has no roof or savings, but a leaf-roofed shelter appeared one rainy week through the kindness of strangers, and he calls it God's doing.
The singer plucks a one-string lute and the leaf drifts down: both are held by the Lord's unseen mercy.
sand doha about God lifting you out of quicksand when you couldn't help yourself
Please write a doha about a man sinking in shifting sand who can neither climb nor call, and the Lord's mercy that lifts him unasked onto firm ground, doing what all his struggling could not.
sand, rescued by mercy
The harder I struggled in the sand, the deeper I sank, until the Lord's mercy raised me.
On a beach trip I stepped into soft wet sand that swallowed me to the knees, and a passer-by pulled me out without a word, and left before I got his name.
skeleton, fire, mercy
skeleton and fire doha about God's mercy beyond even death
My grandmother, who now looks like a skeleton, survived the fire at the care centre which killed others, and she says it was not her doing but a mercy she cannot explain.
Write a doha about a skeleton rescued from fire, or a body saved from ruin, by the Lord's mercy alone, showing that grace can lift even what seems finished and beyond any effort.
Skeleton in the fire, nothing left to offer; and still the Lord's mercy reaches down.
well doha about grace saving someone who fell into a pit
Compose a doha about a man who has fallen into a deep water well and cannot climb out by himself, until the Lord's mercy lowers a hand to him without being asked.
My little brother fell into the old water well when we were children, and a farmer from nowhere pulled him out, and we have never found out who he was.
well, mercy lifted me
Deep in the dark well of my errors I called to no one, yet a hand descended and lifted me.
Our boat was sinking in the dark, our oil press ruined; and then the Lord's mercy arrived, unasked.
boat and oil press doha about God's grace rescuing a family
Please write a doha about a family whose boat has sunk and whose oil press has failed, who have no means of their own left, and who are lifted back up by a mercy they never asked for.
Our boat was wrecked and our oil press burnt in the same month, and I thought we were finished, until neighbours we had never helped rebuilt both without being asked.
boat, oil press, mercy
Lord, You gave me what I never dared to ask, and what I could never have earned.
help unasked, mercy
I never told anyone how bad things had got, and yet help arrived anyway, from the most unexpected people, exactly when I had given up.
Write a doha about the way the Lord's help arrives from unexpected directions, before one has even found the words to ask, and how it does for a person what his own best efforts never could.
doha on how God helped me without me even asking
I tried to rebuild my reputation for years by working harder and harder, and then an apology I never expected from the person who wronged me did it all in a minute.
My long labour was a little stream; Your mercy came like the flood, and carried me.
doha: what hard work couldn't do, God's kindness did in a moment
I want a doha about how the Lord's mercy accomplishes in a single moment what a lifetime of effort could not, and how the person lifted can claim no credit, only gratitude.
mercy in a moment
touchstone, thread, mercy
touchstone and thread doha about God's mercy saving someone who didn't pass the test
The touchstone found my metal base; the thread of mercy still pulled me upward.
Write a doha about a soul that fails every test on the touchstone of merit, but is lifted by a single thread of the Lord's mercy that it never earned and never asked for.
I failed every test they put me through for that job like metal on a touchstone, but a thread of luck, a call from an old friend, got me hired anyway.
grace, not effort
Please write a doha that says that in the end the soul is saved not by its effort or merit but by the Lord's mercy alone, and that the wise man holds out empty hands to receive it.
Empty-handed I came, empty-handed I stand, and still the Lord pours mercy into my palms.
doha on how salvation is by God's grace alone, not my effort
After a lifetime of trying to be good, I realised at sixty that nothing I did had earned the gentle life I have, and that it had all been given.
doha about how the Lord's mercy lifts the lowest of the low
The sweeper in our building was treated badly by everyone, yet when his daughter fell ill, the best doctor in town arrived to treat her for free, and nobody knew who sent him.
You lift the lowest without being asked, Lord, and make the dust a throne.
mercy for the lowest
Compose a doha about the Lord's mercy that finds the lowest and most forgotten person, who has no strength and no merit, and lifts him up gently, unasked, to a place of honour.
My uncle fell into debt and despair, and then the village well dried up; just as he was about to leave, the swan-white rains finally came and everything was saved, he says by grace.
The swan found water in the dry well, though it never knew how; such is the mercy of the Lord.
swan and well doha about God's grace appearing when everything dried up
swan, well, divine mercy
Please write a doha about a swan that finds water in a dry well, with no effort of its own, as the Lord's mercy finds the thirsty soul and gives it what no striving could.
Write a doha about a pot of water that fills itself overnight at the Lord's will, showing how grace gives the soul what it could never gather by effort, however long it laboured.
My pot of water was empty at dawn and brimming by dusk: such is the quiet work of grace.
pot of water, divine grace
pot of water doha about God filling my life when it was empty
When my family was starving after the harvest failed, the village headman quietly sent a pot of water, grain and oil to our gate every week without telling a soul.
